questions.evidence:
Two printing shops advertise notebook-binding services. Shop Green charges thirty dollars to set up a design and ten dollars for each bound notebook. Shop Blue has no setup fee but charges fifteen dollars per notebook. Both use the same paper that the customer supplies.

Riko needs eight notebooks for a club gift project. A friend says Green must be more expensive because its sign shows an extra thirty-dollar fee. Riko writes down both complete calculations instead of comparing only the largest number on each small advertisement.

Green's total for eight notebooks is one hundred and ten dollars. Blue's is one hundred and twenty. Riko confirms that the setup fee is paid once for the shared design, not once per notebook. She also asks whether the quoted totals include all binding charges.

The club chooses Green for this order. Riko does not conclude that Green is cheaper for every order size. With fewer notebooks, the one-time fee could change the comparison. She saves the two price rules, not merely today's winning shop name.
questions.explanation: 需合計固定費與單本費才可比較。
options: The same fee appears at both shops.
The per-notebook prices also affect the full total.
questions.prompt: Why is looking only at the setup fee misleading?
